column1: # No published build shipped the plugin .cfg, in a ZIP or as a launcher-manifest.json seed (every
# seed is BepInEx/config/BepInEx.cfg), so the inputs are what each build writes at its first start.
# A first-run file is the .cfg that build's own SuperliminalHeadTracking.dll, taken from its release
# installer ZIP (each ZIP's SHA-256 checked against the digest GitHub reports for the asset), writes
# when its ConfigManager.Initialize runs on a ConfigFile at a path with no file and the plugin's
# BepInPlugin metadata, as the loader builds it. The Steam DLLs ran under the BepInEx 5 above with the
# Unity stubs of pixi run setup; v0.2.0's Xbox Game Pass DLL ran on .NET 6 under BepInEx 6's
# BepInEx.Core.dll with UnityEngine.CoreModule from the UnityEngine.Modules 2020.3.35 package it was
# built against. The "Acceptable values" comment lines list whichever KeyCode each harness loaded;
# no reader reads a comment line, and they are the only lines where v0.2.0.cfg and
# v0.2.0-il2cpp.cfg differ. The test reads every input with BepInEx 5; the Game Pass build reads the
# .cfg with BepInEx 6 in game, through the same frozen reader compiled against it.
